items.title: A Fundamental Right
items.summary: With its new law that makes education a fundamental right with effect from April 1, 2010, India joins a small group of countries with such a statutory provision. All children in the 6 to 14 age group can exercise the right under the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009. An estimated one crore children who do not go to school now are expected to benefit.

items.title: JSA advises United Spirits on investment in Nuvola Spirits
items.summary: United Spirits Limited has made an investment in Nuvola Spirits Private Limited by way of subscription to 17,350 compulsorily convertible preference shares and 10 equity shares of Nuvola for an aggregate consideration of ₹2.69 crore. JSA Advocates and Solicitors advised United Spirits on this transaction. The transaction was led by Probir Roy Chowdhury (Partner) and Yajas Setlur (Partner), with support from Bhargavi Kuchewar (Senior Associate), Associates Moushami Nayak and Tejaswini Sundar. Nuvola is a craft beverage company behind premium alcoholic brands Mikiamo and Seoulmate, which bring diverse international liquor flavours to the Indian market. The investment forms part of United Spirits strategy to expand its portfolio by backing high-potential, home-grown beverage brands and helping them scale through capital and industry expertise. items.title: CJI Surya Kant declines meeting with Rahul Gandhi, Mallikarjuna Kharge; says approach Court judicially
items.summary: Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant has declined a request by Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi, Mallikarjun Kharge and others to meet him on Monday, October 12, citing the pendency of related matters before the Supreme Court. Sources aware of the development told Bar & Bench that the CJI conveyed that the issues sought to be raised by the Congress leaders were already sub judice before the Supreme Court. The CJI also pointed out that under the constitutional scheme, the Supreme Court does not have administrative powers to interfere with the functioning of the government. Sources said that since the Congress leaders intended to submit a memorandum, the CJI clarified that the Supreme Court could not pass directions on such issues on its administrative side. However, he made it clear that the leaders were free to approach the Supreme Court on its judicial side. Similar matters are already scheduled for hearing before the Supreme Court on Tuesday, October 13. Any petition filed by the Congress leaders could also be heard along with those matters.
